newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa unit chief sees EMU as hurting tourism.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa unit chief sees EMU as hurting tourism.

text.p: While Europe's planned currency union has been touted as having many benefits for European companies, it will hurt the tourism industry, a senior German airline industry official said on Monday.

"The German tourism industry will not be a beneficiary from the common European currency and the industry could suffer immense changes," warned Franz Schoiber, chief executive of Condor Flugdienst GmbH.
Condor is the holiday carrier unit of German national airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG.
Schoiber said the tourism industry had been a main benefactor from the strong mark as it helped to lower dollar denominated prices for goods such as fuel and oil.

"The German tourism industry would not have grown as much as it did in the past years, if we had not been able to benefit from the lower dollar which allowed us to keep prices quite reasonable," Schoiber told a tourism function.
He predicted the firm Euro would "most certainly filter through to tourism prices," in the form of higher prices.
Consequently Schoiber argued that tourism operators based outside the currency union may actually benefit the most from furture developments by being able to keep prices low.
Europe's currency union is scheduled to begin on January 1, 1999.
Schoiber also said his company was particularly cautious about future payments in the common currency.
He said Condor, which recently placed a billion dollars' worth of airplane orders, will probably secure its positions now with marks rather than later with Euros.
